strategyReview: The live book is carried by the proven weekend Hyperliquid funding-reversion family (351/505 live wins, 69.5%, +0.31% avg; 188/253 shadow wins) and the small but excellent one-touch NO live sample (4/4, +18.42% avg). The main failures are in families that take a single static funding reading as a timing signal, use HYPE/listed-IV as directional confirmation, or express a contract-premium edge as a spot move. Those are leaking P&L through unscorable or mismatched tests, and several have already accumulated learned invalid assumptions that must not be repeated.

failureClusters.evidence: CBRS 13/28 (46%), AAPL 10/21 (48%), MU 5/16 (31%); many losses show funding pinned at +5.5% or continuing lower after the trigger, meaning the signal fires after normalization or on non-weekend/stale rows.
failureClusters.recommendation: Refinements must require true weekend timing and lower-tail percentile conditions rather than a standalone < -10% reading; keep the 2-day horizon but only enter genuinely stretched weekend funding states.

failureClusters.evidence: One-touch gold H-534 is 5/19 scorable and burned 7 unscorable tests because the thesis said GOLD spot would decline >2% while the engine grades the contract P&L; many deep NO contracts at 0.93-0.97 produce flat ticks, not spot-like moves.
failureClusters.recommendation: Re-author contract-thesis families as contract premium fades with direction neutral, and never attach a >2% spot prediction to a sell-YES/NO contract test.

failureClusters.evidence: Cross-asset HYPE-BTC confirmation is 9/25 (36%), and BTC listed-IV momentum is 4/18 (22%); H-108 and H-170 have multiple learned invalid assumptions stating HYPE/rising IV do not add independent directional signal.
failureClusters.recommendation: Drop HYPE confirmation for BTC direction, replace it with BTC-owned volatility compression, or convert rising-IV setups to neutral absolute-move/volatility-expansion hypotheses instead of directional long/short bets.

failureClusters.theme: Deep tail NO fade carries tiny tick edge
failureClusters.evidence: GOLD one-touch H-534 examples at 0.93-0.97 NO wins often return +0.0% to +1.1%; the edge is real but tiny and can be erased by spread, while the parent family's spot-decline prediction inflated expectations.
failureClusters.recommendation: Keep one-touch NO fades as contract premium decay, but add tighter spread/liquidity/expiry filters and avoid deep contracts where the edge cannot overcome spread.

newHypotheses.description: Outcome-panel NO edge: buy NO/sell YES across all assets when the best sell-YES model edge is below 1 point and the lowest YES ask is in the mid-price 35-65c band.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on scoped Polymarket contracts is profitable over 7 days as YES overpricing decays; this is a contract P&L thesis, not a spot-direction call.

newHypotheses.description: Sharpest outcome-panel NO cut: buy NO/sell YES across all assets when sell-YES edge is below 1 point, the lowest YES ask is 35-65c, and the nearest contract expires within 30 days.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on near-dated scoped Polymarket contracts is profitable over 7 days as the YES-overpricing edge is strongest near expiry; this is a contract P&L thesis.

newHypotheses.description: Outcome-panel NO edge with tight-spread filter: buy NO/sell YES across all assets when the lowest YES ask is 35-65c and the tightest YES spread is below 2c.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on liquid tight-spread Polymarket contracts is profitable over 7 days as the mid-price YES premium decays; this is a contract P&L thesis.

newHypotheses.description: Outcome-panel NO edge with near-dated filter: buy NO/sell YES across all assets when the lowest YES ask is 35-65c and the nearest contract expires within 30 days.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on near-dated mid-priced Polymarket contracts is profitable over 7 days as the YES premium decays faster near expiry; this is a contract P&L thesis.

newHypotheses.description: Outcome-panel NO edge on above-strike contracts: buy NO/sell YES when one-touch direction is above-strike and the lowest YES ask is in the 35-65c mid-price band.
newHypotheses.prediction: Buying NO / selling YES on above-strike mid-priced Polymarket one-touch contracts is profitable over 7 days as the upside YES premium decays; this is a contract P&L thesis, not a spot call.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-539: replace any-day static CBRS funding < -10 with a true-weekend lower-tail trigger. The original failed on pinned +5.5% and already-normalized funding rows; this enters only when weekend funding is both deeply negative and in the lower 7d tail.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS spot/perp will rise > 2% within 2 days when true-weekend CBRS funding is deeply negative and in the lower tail of its recent range, forcing normalization.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-108: drop HYPE risk-on confirmation and replace it with BTC-owned PM IV compression. HYPE is a coincident BTC beta echo, not an independent signal; compressed BTC PM IV gives a cleaner volatility-expansion setup for continued BTC upside.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot/perp will rise > 2% within 3 days when short-term BTC uptrend coincides with compressed BTC PM IV, without requiring HYPE participation.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-537: restrict AAPL funding reversion to true weekends and require a lower-tail percentile. The original failed on stale funding rows after normalization had already occurred; this enters only when weekend funding is deeply negative and stretched within its own recent range.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL spot will rise > 2% within 2 days when true-weekend AAPL funding is deeply negative and in the lower 7d tail, then mean-reverts.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-534: re-author the gold one-touch cap-edge signal as a contract premium fade instead of a spot-decline prediction. The original burned 7 unscorable tests because the engine grades contract P&L, not GOLD spot movement; keep the large cap-edge trigger but predict YES/NO premium decay.
newHypotheses.prediction: Selling YES / buying NO on scoped GOLD above-strike one-touch contracts is profitable over 3 days as stale cap premium decays; this is a contract P&L thesis, not a GOLD spot-decline call.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H-170: convert the rising-listed-IV momentum setup from a directional long thesis to a neutral absolute-move thesis. The family failed because rising IV did not confirm further BTC gains; the same conditions did, however, often precede large moves in either direction.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will realize an absolute move > 2% within 3 days when spot momentum is confirmed by rising listed option IV; this is a volatility/absolute-move thesis, not a directional long or short.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The any-day standalone CBRS < -10 trigger catches many rows after funding has already normalized or pinned at +5.5%. Wins only cluster when funding is deeply negative and then inflects upward, so the condition lacks timing.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A standalone CBRS funding reading below -10% reliably normalizes within 2 days and forces spot higher.

hypothesisReviews.observation: HYPE risk-on confirmation did not provide independent directional signal; the BTC outcomes were large beta moves in both directions. The family has accumulated multiple learned invalid assumptions that HYPE confirms durable BTC upside.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE risk-on participation independently confirms durable BTC upside rather than late-stage FOMO/overextension.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL < -10 fires on non-weekend and stale rows; losses show funding already at +5.5% or flattening near +0.6%. The static level does not isolate the overstretched weekend funding state the original shadow mined.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: AAPL funding below -10% on any day rapidly normalizes and yields a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The gold one-touch edge is a contract premium phenomenon, not a spot-decline signal. Wins appear as modest NO-contract ticks, losses are flat, and 7 tests were unscorable because the spot-decline prediction did not match the contract instrument.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on gold upside touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Rising listed IV did not confirm further directional BTC gains; the family is 4/18 and shows large adverse moves when graded directionally. The signal is better treated as volatility expansion than as a long-call.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC spot momentum confirmed by rising options IV reliably leads to further >2% gains within 3-7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: MU < -10 mostly captures pinned +5.5% funding rows and lacks true weekend timing; the previous lower-tail refinement was rejected as too rare, so this variant should not be re-proposed in that form.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A single MU funding reading below -10% reliably predicts normalization and a >2% MU spot gain within 2 days.

journalEntry: Tonight's key lesson is that most struggling families are not just weak; they are mechanically mismatched. The funding reversion failures are static-trigger/timing failures, while the contract premium failures are prediction-instrument mismatches. I am sharpening the house YES-overpricing edge with five panel-derived NO variants and making five targeted refinements: weekend-tail timing for CBRS/AAPL, BTC-owned IV compression instead of HYPE confirmation, contract premium fade for gold one-touch, and neutral absolute-move for BTC listed-IV momentum. I also slightly widened FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG stops from 1.5% to 2.0% because the strategy is hitting stops too frequently while its target remains wide.
